articles.title: Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade assure historic medal for India at Asian TT Championships
articles.summary: India’s Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade have secured at least a bronze medal in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent.
articles.body: India’s Harmeet Desai and Yashaswini Ghorpade have secured at least a bronze medal in mixed doubles at the Asian Table Tennis Championships in Tashkent. The Indian pair defeated South Korea’s Park Ganghyeon and Lee Daeun 3-2 in the quarterfinals on Friday to reach the semifinals.Their achievement marks a major milestone for Indian table tennis, as the country has secured a mixed doubles medal at the continental championships for the first time in 72 years. India’s last medal in the event came in 1954.Harmeet and Yashaswini will next take on Japan’s Sora Matsushima and Miwa Harimoto in the semifinals. A victory would send the Indian duo into the final and give them a chance to fight for gold.However, India’s other mixed doubles pair, Payas Jain and Syndrela Das, could not reach the medal stage. They lost 0-3 to China’s Yi Chen and Huang Youzheng in their quarterfinal match.Indian pair looks to make up for Asian Games disappointmentHarmeet and Yashaswini will be hoping to build on their performance after missing out on medals at the recent Asian Games.Harmeet competed in three events at the Games. In the men’s team competition, India reached the round of 16 before losing to South Korea. He and Yashaswini were eliminated in the mixed doubles quarterfinals by China’s Lin Shidong and Kuai Man.Harmeet also partnered Sathiyan Gnanasekaran in men’s doubles, but their campaign ended in the third round after a defeat to Japan’s Sora Matsushima and Shunsuke Togami.Yashaswini also returned without a medal. She lost to Japan’s Miwa Harimoto in the third round of women’s singles. In women’s doubles, she and Diya Chitale reached the quarterfinals but lost 0-3 to China’s Fan Shuhan and Chen Yi.The semifinal now gives Harmeet and Yashaswini an opportunity to secure a historic result for India.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Japan Open: Katie Boulter battles back to beat Antonia Ruzic and reach semi-finals as she reclaims British No 1 spot
articles.summary: Katie Boulter secured an impressive 3-6 6-3 6-3 comeback victory against Antonia Ruzic to reach the Japan Open semi-finals; watch the WTA and ATP Tours live on Sky Sports, with this week's action including events in China, Japan, Kazakhstan, France and Belgium
articles.body:
Boulter got off to a worrying start in a 34-minute first set, unable to wrangle momentum back after losing the first three games of the match in succession and eventually losing 6-3.

The Leicester native, though, showed resilience in the second set, breaking Ruzic's serve three times in a row to force a decider. She trailed 2-0 after being broken in her opening service game, but fought back superbly to level the match.

The world No 58 was then buoyed, winning three games in succession to open the third set and surviving a late Ruzic break to win the final set 6-3 and secure safe passage into the last four.

The result also confirmed her reinstatement as Britain's best female tennis player, just five days after she ceded that mantle due to Sonay Kartal's run to the Wuhan Open final .

Boulter's progress in the tournament overturned her 55-point deficit in the rankings and dethroned Kartal back to the No 2 spot.

"[Ruzic] is a really good player," Boulter said of her opponent in her on-court interview on Sky Sports . "She's extremely tough to beat.

"I did extremely well to come back into it in the second set but she was swinging at everything hard. I felt like anything that I was giving her wasn't bothering her. Full credit to her.

"I tried to hang tough, and in the end I started to play a bit better. I was lucky in the second set, but in the end I felt like I did well to stay there."

Boulter will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in her semi-final match, live on Sky Sports on Saturday.

"[Siniakova is] one hell of a player - she's extremely dangerous," Boulter added. "I know exactly what she's going to bring to the table.

"It's going to be a great match - I've got nothing to lose and I'm going to come prepared tomorrow."

articles.title: Katie Boulter reaches Japan Open semi-final to reclaim British number one ranking
articles.summary: Katie Boulter reclaims the British number one ranking after fighting back to beat Antonia Ruzic in three sets in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open.
articles.body:
Katie Boulter has reclaimed the British number one ranking after fighting back to beat Antonia Ruzic in three sets in the quarter-finals of the Japan Open.

The 30-year-old was dethroned on Monday following Sonay Kartal's run to the final in Wuhan but knew she could overturn the 55-point deficit by reaching the last four in Osaka.

Eighth seed Boulter trailed world number 91 Ruzic by a set and a break but recovered to win 3-6 6-3 6-3 in two hours to reach her first semi-final since Queen's in June.

She will face Czech Katerina Siniakova in the last four and whatever the result will climb above Kartal and back into the world's top 50 when the WTA rankings are updated on Monday.

"[Ruzic] is a really good player, full credit to her," said Boulter. "I tried to hang tough and find a way. I was a bit lucky in the middle of the second [set] but I feel I did really well to stay there."

On facing Siniakova for a spot in the final, she added: "She's one hell of a player, extremely dangerous. It's going to be who gets the first strike in.

"I've got nothing to lose. She's been building extremely well this week, so I'm going to have to come prepared."

Inside British number one Kartal's remarkable comeback

Boulter struggled on serve in the opening two sets, winning just 60% points behind her first serve, hitting four double faults, and facing seven break points, but grew into the match, finding success when stepping inside the baseline to put pressure on the 23-year-old Croat.

Broken in her opening service game, Boulter was gifted a route back into the first set at 4-2 when Ruzic double-faulted on break point. However, Ruzic immediately hit back, winning the next four games.

Boulter wrested back control in an increasingly scrappy second set, saving two break points in the third game to avoid going a double-break down before coming up with a crucial hold in the seventh after the pair had exchanged three successive breaks.

That hold proved the second of eight straight games for Boulter, who raced into a 4-0 lead in the decider. Although she failed to serve out the match at 5-2, she broke her opponent to love to wrap up the win.

Analysis: Boulter's run sets up fascinating British tussle

The immense pride which Kartal felt about becoming the British number one came shining through, describing it as being "up there" in her career achievements.

While she will only initially hold the status for a week, Kartal's impressive comeback and Boulter's decent run creates a fascinating subplot for the leading British women in the final throes of the season - and the start of 2027.

Boulter will have the chance to further improve her ranking when she plays in Tokyo and Hong Kong in the coming weeks, with Kartal's plans for the rest of the season still uncertain as she sensibly manages her workload.

And don't forget about Emma Raducanu. It seems increasingly unlikely she will play again this season because of the shin injury which ruled her out of Wimbledon, but is clearly too good a player not to be pushing back into the top 50 when she does return.

When all three are back competing on the WTA Tour at the same time, it promises to be an interesting tussle between them in the rankings.

Boulter and Raducanu both insisted they were not transfixed by the British number one spot when they exchanged positions in 2025, instead preferring to focus on their own career paths and the bigger picture of the world rankings.

But there is no doubt that Boulter, in particular, could see the opportunity to cement her place as the nation's best player as an extra incentive to continue finishing 2026 strongly.
